Digital Currency & Wholesale CBDCs: Project [Project mBridge](https://www.bis.org/about/bisih/topics/cbdc/mcbdc.htm) has advanced from proof-of-concept to commercial reality, evidenced by Industrial Bank and Bank of China executing multi-billion-dollar transactions and significant equity acquisitions. Financial Market Infrastructure & Correspondent Banking: The emergence of local-currency stablecoins and the completion of Nasdaq’s de-risking cycle indicate a structural shift toward optimizing existing architectures rather than wholesale exit strategies. We provide advisory support for optimizing treasury workflows and navigating PBOC regulatory frameworks to ensure seamless trade finance execution across these new channels.

Emerging Market Infrastructure: Ethiopia faces critical de-risking challenges that hinder its integration into global settlement architecture, requiring modernized, transparent channels to meet international benchmarks. There is a clear mandate to map domestic settlement rails to [Project mBridge](https://www.bis.org/about/bisih/topics/cbdc/mcbdc.htm)-compatible architectures, effectively bridging local liquidity with multi-currency wholesale CBDC networks. We are currently proposing phased advisory engagements to help local firms align their infrastructure with these global digital standards.

insights.title: RMB cross-border payments system launched in Kenya to boost Sino-Africa trade - Xinhua

This fosters greater financial autonomy for participating nations and potentially reduces FX conversion costs and settlement times.
* **Consulting Pivot:** Advise African financial institutions and corporations on optimizing treasury operations and trade finance workflows to leverage direct RMB clearing through CIPS, including integration strategies, FX risk management, and compliance with Chinese regulatory frameworks for trade.

This indicates opportunities for financial technology providers to offer solutions that integrate with or enhance CIPS capabilities for Standard Bank and other African financial institutions, particularly in transaction processing, compliance, and reporting. Potential partners could include specialized payment gateway providers, trade finance platforms, or regulatory technology (RegTech) firms.
insight.mets_rationalization: This development directly links to the long-term trend of de-dollarization and the internationalization of the Renminbi. The expansion of CIPS as a direct settlement rail for Sino-African trade diversifies global payment infrastructure, reducing systemic reliance on legacy correspondent banking networks and offering a more efficient, direct clearing mechanism for RMB-denominated transactions. This aligns with the hub's interest in tracking the evolution of sovereign payment rails and their impact on global financial flows.
